title: Text in a binary
description: The runs of printable characters a binary carries, with where each one lies: an offset for a hex editor, an address for a disassembler, and the section that maps one to the other. What counts as printable is strings(1)'s set — 0x20 to 0x7E plus tab — and a run needs no terminator, because a literal that fills its section has none.

file.description: Path of the binary as it was given.

format.description: pe32, pe64, elf32, elf64 or macho: what the file's own magic says it is. Null when no loader claimed it, in which case the whole file was scanned and no rva is reported.

strings.description: One entry per run, in the order they lie in the file.

offset.description: Offset in the file, counted from zero.

rva.description: Address in the loaded image, when a section maps the offset. Null for a run in a header or an overlay, which is not loaded.

section.description: The section the run lies in; empty when none does.

encoding.description: One byte per character, or two little-endian.

length.description: Characters in the run, which is not the same as bytes for utf16.

bytes.description: Bytes the run occupies in the file.

text.description: The characters themselves, verbatim: they may contain tab.

reported.description: Runs in this document, after any filter.

found.description: Runs the scan found, before any filter: larger than reported means the filter dropped some.

distinct.description: Distinct texts among the runs found: how much of the file's text is repetition.

bytes_scanned.description: Bytes the scan covered: the whole file, or one section when one was named.

min_length.description: The shortest run that was reported, which is the threshold that was in force.

sections_scanned.description: Sections the scan covered, in file order; empty when the file is not one whose sections are known, in which case the whole file was scanned.

problems.description: Anything that stopped the reading from being complete, said rather than swallowed.
